ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)

clock_waveform.SWCLK_role: Serial Wire Clock. Generated by the debug host. Free-running during a transaction; may be stopped between transactions (the SW-DP wire-level FSM idles when SWCLK stops).
clock_waveform.rising_edge: Target samples SWDIO during Request and Data-Write phases. SWD wire-level FSM advances on this edge.
clock_waveform.falling_edge: Target drives SWDIO during ACK and Data-Read phases so that the host samples cleanly on the next rising edge.
clock_waveform.frequency_range: Typical 1-50 MHz; some probes go to 100 MHz or 50% of the target's HCLK. Implementation-defined per target. Cortex-M0+ targets typically clamp at 10 MHz; Cortex-A targets at 50+ MHz.

swdio_waveform.SWDIO_role: Bidirectional serial data. Host-driven during Request and Data-Write phases; target-driven during ACK and Data-Read phases; tri-state during Turnaround periods (briefly).

drive_direction_table.driver: same as Data phase (host on write, target on read)

swdio_waveform.park_bit_behavior: Bit 7 of the Request (Park=1) drives SWDIO HIGH before the host releases the line — this gives the bus a known HIGH level during the Turnaround A period.
swdio_waveform.idle_level: Recommended HIGH between transactions so that the line-reset condition is approached if the host loses contact.

reset_waveform.line_reset_sequence: SWDIO held HIGH for at least 50 consecutive SWCLK rising edges from any state forces SW-DP to Idle / reset state.
reset_waveform.selection_sequence_swd_to_jtag: 16-bit pattern 0xE73C (LSB first on SWDIO) preceded by ≥ 50 cycles of SWDIO=HIGH and followed by ≥ 50 cycles of SWDIO=HIGH; switches SWJ-DP from SWD mode to JTAG mode.
reset_waveform.selection_sequence_jtag_to_swd: 16-bit pattern 0xE79E (LSB first on TMS) preceded by ≥ 50 cycles of TMS=HIGH and followed by ≥ 50 cycles of TMS=HIGH; switches SWJ-DP from JTAG mode to SWD mode.

transaction_waveform_summary: Host drives SWDIO from idle (HIGH) and begins the Request: bits 0..7 LSB-first on SWCLK rising edges (Start=1, APnDP, RnW, A[2], A[3], Parity, Stop=0, Park=1).
Park=1 leaves SWDIO HIGH; host tri-states; Turnaround A (1 SWCLK cycle by default).
Target drives the 3-bit ACK on the falling edges of the next 3 SWCLKs (host samples on the next rising edges).

If ACK=OK: for a Read, target drives the next 32 SWDIO cycles with the data LSB-first (falling-edge drive, host samples rising); after 32 bits, target drives the parity bit; then Turnaround B; host resumes drive.
If ACK=OK: for a Write, host drives the next 32 SWDIO cycles with the data LSB-first (host drives on falling, target samples on rising); after 32 bits, host drives the parity bit; then Turnaround B.
If ACK=WAIT or FAULT: host should treat the next 32+1 bits as junk (typically all zeros), then drive Turnaround B and either retry (WAIT) or read CTRL/STAT + ABORT (FAULT).
Between transactions, host may either keep SWDIO HIGH or release it; common probes idle SWCLK low and SWDIO high.
posted_read_waveform_summary: Host issues Read of AP register N: ACK=OK; receives 32 bits of data on SWDIO — but this data is actually the result of the previous AP read, or implementation-defined garbage on the first read of a sequence.
Host issues second Read of AP register: receives the actual data of read N.
To recover the last read of a burst, host reads DP.RDBUFF (APnDP=0, A[3:2]=0xC, RnW=1); the ACK returns the OK of the last AP read; the data field returns the read-N data.

Pipelining note: hosts typically issue the next Read while the previous read is still propagating through the AP layer; this hides the AP transaction latency at the cost of one extra trailing RDBUFF read.

rows: SWDIO target drive delay (from SWCLK falling)
timing_parameters_per_device.notes: ADIv5 does not specify absolute values; per-device datasheets do. Most modern Cortex-M MCUs support SWCLK up to ~24 MHz; SoCs with CoreSight DAP support up to ~50 MHz; some high-end Cortex-A SoCs support up to 100 MHz with adaptive clocking.
